title: Best of Vietnam in 14 days
summary: Hanoi, one northern landscape, Hue, Hoi An, and Ho Chi Minh City. Fly at least once. Add the Mekong only if you drop a northern night.

days.title: Day 1 — Old Quarter
days.body: Land in Hanoi and walk the Old Quarter north of Hoan Kiem Lake.

days.title: Day 2 — Lake and citadel
days.body: Walk Hoan Kiem Lake, see the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long, and eat bun cha.

days.title: Day 4 — Ninh Binh or Ha Long
days.body: Take the sampan through the three caves at Tam Coc, or take a boat on Ha Long Bay, and do not do both.

days.title: Day 5 — Leave Hanoi
days.body: Return to Hanoi, then fly to Hue the next morning or board the sleeper train.

days.title: Day 6 — Hue Citadel
days.body: Visit the Hue Citadel and eat bun bo Hue.

days.title: Day 7 — Hue tombs
days.body: Visit the tombs of Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh.

days.title: Day 8 — Hoi An
days.body: Travel to Hoi An, add Hai Van Pass only in clear weather, and walk the old town from the Japanese Covered Bridge.

days.title: Day 10 — An Bang or My Son
days.body: Spend the day at An Bang Beach, or at the My Son towers.

days.title: Day 11 — Ho Chi Minh City
days.body: Fly from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City and walk the center.

days.title: Day 13 — Can Tho or Cu Chi
days.body: Go on to Can Tho, or to the Cu Chi tunnels if you are flying home from the city.

days.title: Day 14 — Cai Rang
days.body: Be at Cai Rang at dawn if you came south, or fly home if you stayed in the city.

seoDescription: A practical 14-day route from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City, with one northern side trip and the central coast.
